subject: Optimizing the TPEQD projection in CTMM

messages.author: 7c8a33455cb7050c
messages.subject: Optimizing the TPEQD projection in CTMM
parts:
Hi Chris!  

Can you elaborate on how CTMM optimizes the Two Point Equidistant projection?  I combed thru some of the code on GitHub but couldn't find anything.  

I do believe it is the optimal projection for my study area as  I compared the distortion on distance calculations across several projections and the TPEQD projection performed the best. However, I would like to understand how ctmm comes to this dataset-specific specification of the projection, specifically how are the "two points" are chosen. Are these optimized to reduce error?  

For my work, I coerced my data (in WGS84) into a large MoveStack, and then used as.telemetry() to coerce it into a list of telemetry objects. 
Examining the projection info for each object shows they are all the same.  

DATA.trj[[1]]@info$projection
"+proj=tpeqd +lat_1=64.2001964300436 +lon_1=-112.523229163276 +lat_2=65.7643765449217 +lon_2=-111.041601376637 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"

When I plot these lat_1,long_1 & lat_2, long2, they are somewhat central to the entire dataset (screenshot shows them overtop of the telemetry dataset of ~300 hundred caribous over several years).  How does CTMM pick these points?  




Thanks, Robin

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Optimizing the TPEQD projection in CTMM
parts:
Hi Robin,

I take the (x,y,z) locations in 3D Euclidean space (not constrained to the ellipsoid) and perform k=2 geometric median clustering with the Gmedian package, which is a form of clustering that is robust to outliers. I then take the two cluster medians and project them down to the ellipsoid (though, typically they won't be far from the ellipsoid). With multiple individuals, I do this once per individual and then again on all of the individual cluster locations to prevent over-fitting to the better sampled individuals. The code is in median.R: https://github.com/ctmm-initiative/ctmm/blob/master/R/median.R

With the TPEQD projection, distances from either focus are accurate. So, if you have a big migration, then the projection can still be relatively accurate. In cases like yours, where you don't have a big migration, then you just get two points in the bulk of the data. Usually these two points span the larger extent of the data, which is what you want.

Best,
Chris
